Date: Fri, May 20, 2016 at 12:14 PM
Subject: Re: Problems with phylobase package


Hi XXX -- I'm not a phylobase developer, I've never had a problem really, but then I've never used Kubuntu.

You are kind of in "dependency hell", but what you should do is go through each of those dependency packages and get them installed first.  Then try phylobase again, if new dependencies come up, get those installed first, etc.  Then if there are remaining issues, try to figure those out or email the phylobase developers.

But -- BioGeoBEARS only uses a tiny bit of phylobase, basically the phylo4 object gets used a bit, I think for prt etc.  You could try to just find the code for that and load it, and then just load all of the source() files on the BioGeoBEARS example script, which has all of the BioGeoBEARS code at this point. This won't have the help files, but those aren't up to date anyway.  (You will still need packages rexpokit and cladoRcpp installed.)

Cheers, Nick

messages.author: e06588dcdd0dbfaa
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Fwd: Problems with phylobase package
parts:
Hi,

I've no experience with Kubunutu, but on Ubuntu I had to install some
additional libraries: my suggestions would be something like libssl-dev
and libcurl4-nss-dev (on Ubuntu, dev-libararies are often not installed
by default). Once openssl and curl compile normally, all the other
packages, including phylobase, should compile fine.
Hope that helps.

Best
Gerald

messages.author: 97fe942905e4bb14
messages.subject: Re: Problems with phylobase package
parts:
Hello,

I also had this problem with Linux Ubuntu. I solved it by adding 2 additional libraries, lib32z1-dev and libxml2-dev, as well as Gerald's suggestions (libssl-dev and libcurl4-nss-dev).  libxml2-dev was suggested by R to download in the error messages, but I had to download lib32z1-dev first. 


sudo apt-get install lib32z1-dev
sudo apt-get install libxml2-dev
